the polarization mechanism of high-temperature electrolysis in solid oxide cells.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polarization mechanism of high temperature solid oxide electrolysis is similar to the fuel cell operation except for the opposite chemical potential variation of the reactants.

the polarization behavior of the high temperature solid oxide electrolysis cells is mainly determined by the chemical potential gradients of the reactants/products, which is consistent with the general characteristics of the gas electrodes, and the gas concentration impedance of the Ni-YSZ electrode is the main contributor to the polarization losses.
the Ni–YSX electrode is co-limited by the gas-phase and surface diffusion and reaction, while the LSM electrode is co-limitied by the surface diffusion and chemical capacitance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the polarization mechanism in a Ni–YSZ cathode and an LSM anode of a solid oxide electrolysis cell is quite distinct from the polarization mechanism in fuel cells.

the high temperature electrolytic polarization can be consistently explained as the consequence of the chemical potential changes of the reactants/products, while the polarization mechanism of the fuel cell can be attributed to the charge-transfer process.
the polarization behavior of the high temperature solid oxide electrolysis can be explained by the chemical-potential-driven surface reaction and diffusion process of the gas electrodes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the electrolysis and fuel cell polarization of the Ni–Yttria stabilized ZrO 2 (Ni–YSZ)/YSZ/La 0.8 Sr 0.2 MnO 3 (LSM) solid oxide cells can be consistently explained with the same polarization mechanism.
the polarization behavior of solid oxide cells is not only a function of the electrode material, but is also strongly dependent on the electrolysis current density and the operating conditions.

the polarization behavior of high temperature electrolyzers can be systematically explained by the chemical capacitance of gas electrode, which is a general characteristic of the solid oxide cells, and can be quantitatively evaluated by the finite-length Gerischer modeling.
